newsitem.title: MEXICO: PRI lead shrinks in three Mexican states - poll.
newsitem.headline: PRI lead shrinks in three Mexican states - poll.

text.p: Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) faces a shrinking lead in three elections for state governor next month, according to a new opinion poll published on Thursday.

Though the PRI still enjoys a commanding -- albeit diminishing -- lead in the impoverished southeastern state of Campeche, its support dropped sharply in the northern states of San Luis Potosi and Sonora, the Reforma poll said.
The three states are among six that will hold elections for governor on July 6, when Mexicans will pick a new Congress, a quarter of the Senate and a mayor of Mexico City.
The PRI's 68-year majority in the Chamber of Deputies is considered under threat in the elections, and nationwide its perfomance is expected to be the poorest in its history.

Between May and June in San Luis Potosi, the PRI's lead dropped 13 points to 30 percent, while the opposition National Action Party (PAN) inched up to 23 percent, the poll said. Undecided voters or those who planned not to vote were the largest section of those surveyed in the state.
In Sonora, where it had held a steady 40 percent since February, the PRI's support suddenly sank to 31 percent in June, the poll showed.

Most of the difference was made up for by the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), which traditionally had little clout in the north. Its backing rose from 12 to 17 percent, the poll said.

In Campeche, the PRD also saw a slight increase, to 31 percent from 28 percent, but the PRI remained well in front at 41 percent, just one point lower than its level the last time a survey was taken on June 2.
The poll was carried out with more than 1,000 interviewees in each state between June 19 and 22, Reforma daily said. It had a margin of error of 3.5 percent.
